report_narrative: One of four fictional claims is supported within the supplied registry scope. The license claim is contradicted, the staffing claim has one upstream origin, and the award identity is unresolved; one planned search remains access-limited.
The review tests four propositions about fictional AQ-104 against six supplied items and five planned searches. Four searches were completed; the absent court docket remains a coverage gap.
F-01: Fictional D-02 claims a current license while D-03 records expiration for AQ-104.
F-02: D-02, D-04, and D-05 repeat one company assertion of 240 employees.
F-03: D-06 names AQ-901 rather than target AQ-104.

The active registry entry supports legal status at its cutoff only. The licensing statement is contradicted, the 240-employee assertion has only one upstream origin, and the award cannot be attributed across different registration identifiers.

Five of six reviewed items are eligible for the subject. Three staffing publications count as one source family. Completing four of five searches gives 80.0% planned-search completion, with no claim about the completeness of the public record.
SYN-001 resolves to D-01 through D-06 and the search plan in file 10. D-03 contradicts the licensing claim; D-06 identifies AQ-901 rather than AQ-104. No court outcome is evidenced.
Prioritize current licensing evidence, independent staffing support, and the missing docket. Keep the award excluded unless identity linkage is demonstrated.
